cards.text: God is still talking to Moses up on the mountain (Exodus 24:18; 25:1), laying out how to build Him a sanctuary so He can dwell among them (Exodus 25:8). He's already covered the ark, the table and the lampstand (Exodus 25:10-40). Now He gets to the tabernacle itself: ten curtains of fine linen, with blue, purple and scarlet yarn.

cards.question: God says to skillfully work ___ into those ten linen curtains.

cards.text: The ten curtains get joined into two sets of five, with fifty blue loops lined up along the edge of each set. Fifty loops, friend, lined up PERFECTLY, and I can't even get two sprinkles to sit straight.

cards.question: God says to hook the two linen sets together with fifty gold clasps. Why?

answers.text: So the tabernacle is one unit
So the light can shine through
So each set can stand alone

cards.text: Over the tabernacle goes a tent of goat hair, eleven curtains this time, one more than the linen. That's me with chocolate chips, friend. The recipe says ten, and I'm ALWAYS grabbing eleven.

cards.question: The extra goat hair gets trimmed off so the tent fits neat and tidy.

cards.text: On top of the goat hair goes a covering of ram skins dyed red, and over that, a covering of fine leather. That tent is wearing more layers than me, friend, and I've got an apron, a neckerchief AND a hat.

Then come the walls: acacia frames, twenty on each long side and eight at the back, every one standing on silver bases, braced with crossbars and overlaid with gold. I spent years in a junk drawer next to old instruction manuals, friend, and not ONE of them had silver bases.
Then God tells Moses to set it all up a certain way. It's the way Moses was already shown, right there on the mountain.

cards.question: God says to set up the tabernacle according to the ___ shown to Moses on the mountain.

cards.text: Next comes a veil of blue, purple and scarlet yarn and fine linen, with cherubim worked into it. It hangs on gold hooks from four gold-covered posts standing on silver bases.

cards.question: What does God say to place behind that veil?
The veil splits the tabernacle into two rooms. The front one is the Holy Place. What is the room behind the veil?
God says to put the mercy seat on top of the ark of the Testimony, there in the Most Holy Place.
Where does God say to put the table and the lampstand?

answers.text: Outside the veil across from each other
Behind the veil on each side of the ark
Side by side next to the entrance

cards.text: Then a curtain for the entrance to the tent, embroidered with blue, purple and scarlet yarn and fine linen. It hangs from five gold-covered posts with gold hooks.

cards.question: The five posts at the tent's entrance stand on silver bases, just like the wall frames.

cards.text: Next God lays out an altar of acacia wood, square, five cubits on each side and three cubits high. I stand on a gold base, friend, and I STILL couldn't see over that thing.

cards.question: God says to make a ___ on each of the altar's four corners, all one piece with it.

cards.text: The altar gets its tools too: pots for the ashes, shovels, sprinkling bowls, meat forks and firepans. This altar comes with a whole tool set, friend, and I'm over here with one mustache.

cards.question: The altar is overlaid with ___, and all its tools are made of it too.

cards.text: A bronze mesh grate sits under the altar's ledge, halfway up, with a bronze ring at each corner. Then acacia poles overlaid with bronze slide into the rings, one on each of two sides.

cards.question: Why do those bronze-covered poles go through the altar's rings?

answers.text: So the altar can be carried
So the grate can be lifted out
So the altar can be tied down

cards.question: God says to build the altar out of boards so it's solid all the way through.

cards.text: Then God marks out a courtyard with walls of fine linen on posts, a hundred cubits on the north and south and fifty on the west. On the east side, toward the sunrise, fifteen cubits of curtain go on each end.

cards.question: On the courtyard's east side, between those two stretches of curtain, what fills the middle?
The curtain on the courtyard gate is plain linen with no colors worked into it.

cards.text: Every courtyard post gets silver hooks and bronze bases, and even the tent pegs are bronze. The TENT PEGS, friend, and I've never gotten instructions this detailed for ANY batch.
Then God tells Moses to command the Israelites to bring pure oil of pressed olives for the light.

cards.question: How often are the lamps supposed to keep burning with that oil?
In the Tent of Meeting, outside the veil, who does God say will tend the lamps?

cards.text: Aaron is Moses' brother (Exodus 4:14), and now he and his sons are on lamp duty. After years in a dark drawer, friend, a job all about keeping the light ON sounds wonderful to me.

cards.question: Aaron and his sons tend the lamps before the LORD from evening until morning.
God says tending the lamps is only for while Israel is out in the wilderness.

cards.text: "This is to be a permanent statute for the Israelites for the generations to come." But God's not done talking to Moses up on that mountain, friend, so keep your apron on.

findings.problem: The whole passage, Exodus 26:1-27:21, is building plans for the tabernacle, the altar and the courtyard. The long-stretch rule names exactly this kind of material: one summary story card, no choice cards and never a stop of its own. The walkthrough instead gives the passage two full stops and 19 choice cards. It treats only Exodus 26:15-29 as a long stretch and quizzes the rest of the plans, such as the clasps, the bases, the bronze, the hollow altar and the gate curtain.
findings.question: When a whole passage is a long stretch, like the tabernacle building plans, how should the walkthrough handle it? Should it be one summary card, should some of the plans get choice cards, or is another approach intended? Also, should the rule against stops of their own and choice cards for long stretches apply when nothing else is in the passage?

findings.problem: The setup says God tells Moses to set it all up 'a certain way,' 'the way Moses was already shown.' Card 10 then asks for the ___ shown to Moses. Calling it 'a way' points to 'pattern' and rules out the wrong answers 'promise' and 'warning,' because neither one is a way to set something up.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The joke 'The recipe says ten, and I'm ALWAYS grabbing eleven' compares the eleven goat-hair curtains to going past the instructions. But God's instructions call for eleven on purpose (Exodus 26:7). Following a plan that asks for one more is a different action from ignoring a recipe and grabbing extra.

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.

findings.problem: Card 17 has just asked and answered that tending the lamps is permanent, not only for the wilderness. Card 18 then repeats the same point by quoting 'This is to be a permanent statute...' before the story-continues line. That makes the card a recap. Because the last verse was already asked on a choice card, this card can be only the story-continues line.
